lines: Sequencer driven by a chaotic map: an iterated function is stepped once per clock, and the section of the map its value falls in fires the CV, GATE and TRIG jacks belonging to that section
Chooses the function that is iterated: the logistic map at 0, the tent map at 1, the parabola at 2
Sets how many times the function is applied to its own result on each clock step, 1 to 7
Sets the bifurcation parameter over a range of 0 to 10, which is the growth rate fed to the function: 2.5 to 3.99 for the logistic map, 1.0 to 1.99 for the tent and the parabola
Adds to the r(t) knob, one unit of its 0 to 10 range per volt, and the total is clamped to that range
Sets the rate of the internal clock, doubling per step from 15 bpm at -2 to 3840 bpm at 6, and it has no effect while EXT is patched
Adds to the CLK knob, doubling the internal clock rate per volt, and it has no effect while EXT is patched
A rising edge steps the function once and takes over from the internal clock; it reads high at 1V and low at 0V
Splits the map into 1, 2, 4 or 8 sections, which sets how many jacks share a section: at 1 every jack is active at once, at 8 only the jacks of one section are
The position of the current point within the section this jack belongs to, 0V at the bottom of that section rising to 10V at the top, held at its last value while the point is elsewhere
10V while the current point falls inside the section this jack belongs to, 0V while it is elsewhere
A 1ms pulse of 10V each time the point arrives in the section this jack belongs to
Note — the internal clock runs from the moment the module is added, so the outputs move with nothing patched; a cable in EXT replaces that clock
Note — the COBWEB DIAGRAM draws the shape of the chosen function with its latest iteration points, and the BIFURCATION MAP draws where the point has been falling; neither takes a click
TheBifurcator.notes: The output jacks are numbered from the bottom of the panel upwards: CV index 0 is the lowest row and index 7 the top row, and the same for the GATE and TRIG columns. A CV jack keeps its last voltage when its section is not the active one; the code that would zero it is commented out.

lines: Slow CV source: a four-dimensional cube turns in six planes and is projected onto a flat plane, and the X and Y coordinates of each of its sixteen vertices come out as a voltage
Sets how fast the cube turns in the XY plane, stopped at 0 and about one turn every six seconds at 1
Sets how fast the cube turns in the YZ plane, stopped at 0 and about one turn every six seconds at 1
Sets how fast the cube turns in the XZ plane, stopped at 0 and about one turn every six seconds at 1
Sets how fast the cube turns in the YW plane, stopped at 0 and about one turn every six seconds at 1
Sets how fast the cube turns in the XW plane, stopped at 0 and about one turn every six seconds at 1
Sets how fast the cube turns in the ZW plane, stopped at 0 and about one turn every six seconds at 1
Sets the viewing distance used for the perspective projection, 1.5 to 8; a shorter distance spreads the vertices further apart and widens the swing of every output
Adds to the XY knob, each volt turning that plane as fast again as the knob at its maximum
Adds to the YZ knob, each volt turning that plane as fast again as the knob at its maximum
Adds to the XZ knob, each volt turning that plane as fast again as the knob at its maximum
Adds to the YW knob, each volt turning that plane as fast again as the knob at its maximum
Adds to the XW knob, each volt turning that plane as fast again as the knob at its maximum
Adds to the ZW knob, each volt turning that plane as fast again as the knob at its maximum
Adds to the DISTANCE knob, a tenth of a unit per volt, and the total is clamped to 1.5 to 8
The X coordinate of that vertex in the projection, 0V at the far left of the plot rising to 10V at the far right, refreshed about 1024 times a second
The Y coordinate of that vertex in the projection, running from 0V at one edge of the plot to 10V at the other, refreshed about 1024 times a second
Note — all six rotation knobs start at zero, so the cube does not turn and every output holds one voltage until a rotation knob is raised or a rotation CV is patched
Tesseract.notes: Output indices 0 to 15 are the X coordinate of vertices 1 to 16 and indices 16 to 31 the Y coordinate of the same vertices; on the panel each vertex is one coloured row, the first eight in the left pair of columns and the last eight in the right pair. The vertical direction of the Y outputs was not established: the projected coordinate is mapped from -1 to 1 onto 0-10V, but which end of the plot that is drawn at was not checked.

lines: Chaotic CV source: the Ikeda map is stepped once per clock and the X and Y coordinates of each new point come out as voltages
Sets the u parameter of the map over 0.6 to 0.9, which sets how far each step rotates and contracts and how ragged the attractor becomes
Adds to the u knob, a twentieth of a unit per volt, and the total is clamped to 0.6 to 0.9
Weights the angle term of the map over 0.25 to 3.5, which reshapes the attractor without changing the clock
Adds to the t knob, half a unit per volt, and the total is clamped to 0.25 to 3.5
Sets the rate of the internal clock, doubling per step from 15 bpm at -2 to 3840 bpm at 6, and it has no effect while EXT is patched
A rising edge steps the map once and takes over from the internal clock; it reads high at 1V and low at 0V
Adds to the CLK knob, doubling the internal clock rate per volt, and it has no effect while EXT is patched
Sets the full-scale voltage of the X-CV output, 0 to 10V
Sets the full-scale voltage of the Y-CV output, 0 to 10V
The X coordinate of the newest point, 0V where x is -1.5 and rising to the full-scale voltage set by its LEVEL knob where x is 2.5, clamped outside that
The Y coordinate of the newest point, inverted: 0V where y is 2 and rising to the full-scale voltage set by its LEVEL knob where y is -2, clamped outside that
Note — the internal clock runs from the moment the module is added, so the outputs move with nothing patched; a cable in EXT replaces that clock
Oscillator that traces a rhodonea, or rose, curve at audio rate and sends the X and Y coordinates of the tracing point out as two waveforms
Sets the numerator of the n over d ratio in whole steps from 1 to 10, which sets the number of petals on the rose and the frequency of the harmonic it adds
Adds to the n knob, one unit per volt, and the total is clamped to 1 to 10
Sets the denominator of the n over d ratio in whole steps from 1 to 10, which sets the number of petals on the rose and the frequency of the harmonic it adds
Adds to the d knob, one unit per volt, and the total is clamped to 1 to 10
Crossfades from the full rose curve at 0 to a plain sine at the set pitch at 1
Adds to the a knob, a tenth per volt, and the total is clamped to 0 to 1
Sets the frequency over -4 to 4, an octave per step, with 0 giving C4 at 261.63Hz
Adds to the pitch knob at a volt per octave, and the total is clamped to -4V to 4V
Rotates the curve through up to a full turn, which shifts the phase of both outputs by the same amount
Rotates the curve, a full turn over 10V, added to the angle knob and clamped to one turn
The Y coordinate of the tracing point, ±5V through a 20Hz high-pass filter, marked on the panel by the pink axis of the plot
The X coordinate of the tracing point, ±5V through a 20Hz high-pass filter, marked on the panel by the cyan axis of the plot
Note — both outputs run through one filter instance, processed one after the other in the same sample, so patching X and Y at once puts the two signals through a single shared filter state
Rhodonea.notes: Both outputs are filtered by one shared BiquadFilter instance, processed one after the other in the same sample, so patching X and Y at once interleaves the two signals through a single filter state. The maker's tooltip calls the pitch and angle knobs 'pitch CV' and 'angle (phase) CV' although they are knobs; the panel prints pitch and angle.

notes: No module in this plugin calls appendContextMenu, so there are no menu lines to write; the right-click menu carries only Rack's own items. Checked against the maker's source, which matches the installed 2.0.0. Knob defaults read from configParam: Tesseract's six rotation knobs default to 0, which is why it sits still when first added; The Bifurcator and Ikeda default their clock knob to 2, so both run on their own. No display in the plugin handles a click or a drag.
